# Installing Maned

Maned ships as prebuilt binaries for macOS and Linux. There is nothing to
compile and no runtime to install first.

## Quick install

```sh
curl -fsSL https://fabianodicheti.github.io/maned/install.sh | sh
```

That downloads the right build for your machine, verifies its SHA-256 against
the release manifest, and installs three commands. It never uses `sudo` and
never edits your shell configuration.

Then check it worked:

```sh
maned-run --version
```

```
maned-run 0.1.1
build: b6c94fa (aarch64-apple-darwin)
```

If the command is not found, see [PATH](#the-command-is-not-found) below.

## With Homebrew

On macOS or Linuxbrew:

```sh
brew install fabianodicheti/maned/maned
```

Upgrading later:

```sh
brew update && brew upgrade maned
```

## What gets installed

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `maned-run` | run a `.mnd` program, locally or on remote workers |
| `maned-serve` | serve one `.mnd` script as an HTTP API |
| `maned-lint` | static checks, with diagnostics an editor can parse |

By default they go to `/usr/local/bin` if you can write there, and
`~/.local/bin` otherwise.

## Installer options

```sh
# install a specific release instead of the latest
curl -fsSL https://fabianodicheti.github.io/maned/install.sh | sh -s -- --version 0.1.1

# install somewhere else
curl -fsSL https://fabianodicheti.github.io/maned/install.sh | sh -s -- --prefix ~/tools

# show what would happen, change nothing
curl -fsSL https://fabianodicheti.github.io/maned/install.sh | sh -s -- --dry-run

# remove it again
curl -fsSL https://fabianodicheti.github.io/maned/install.sh | sh -s -- --uninstall
```

If you would rather read the script before running it — which is a reasonable
thing to want:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://fabianodicheti.github.io/maned/install.sh -o install.sh
less install.sh
sh install.sh
```

## Installing by hand

Download a tarball from the
[releases page](https://github.com/FabianoDicheti/maned/releases), then:

```sh
tar -xzf maned-0.1.1-<target>.tar.gz
cd maned-0.1.1-<target>
sudo cp bin/* /usr/local/bin/                      # everyone
mkdir -p ~/.local/bin && cp bin/* ~/.local/bin/    # just you
```

`<target>` is one of `universal-apple-darwin`, `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, or
`aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`.

To verify the download yourself, get `SHA256SUMS` from the same release and:

```sh
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS --ignore-missing     # Linux
shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS --ignore-missing # macOS
```

## Your first program

```sh
cat > hello.mnd <<'EOF'
mnd::quantmax=1000;
mnd::quantmin=-1000;
mnd::quantres=0;

in::a = 2;
in::b = 3;
in::c = 4;

calc::lambda_flow arithmetic(a, b, c) {
    a b add c mul sum_then_scale =   # (2 + 3) * 4 = 20
    b c mul a add scale_then_sum =   # 2 + (3 * 4) = 14
} return sum_then_scale, scale_then_sum;
EOF

maned-run hello.mnd
```

```
flow 'arithmetic' outputs:
sum_then_scale : scalar = 20
scale_then_sum : scalar = 14
```

Maned is postfix: no operator precedence and no parentheses. Those two lines
use the same three values and the same two operators — only the token order
differs.

## Editor support

A VS Code extension provides syntax highlighting and a `.mnd` file icon.
Download `maned-lang-0.1.1.vsix` from the
[releases page](https://github.com/FabianoDicheti/maned/releases) and:

```sh
code --install-extension maned-lang-0.1.1.vsix
```

Or in VS Code: **Extensions** → `…` menu → **Install from VSIX…**

Syntax highlighting works immediately. The **file icon needs one more step**,
because VS Code file icons come entirely from the active icon theme and an
extension cannot add an entry to a theme it does not own.

If you use Material Icon Theme, add to `settings.json`:

```jsonc
"material-icon-theme.files.associations": { "*.mnd": "haskell" }
```

If you use vscode-icons:

```jsonc
"vsicons.associations.files": [
  { "icon": "haskell", "extensions": ["mnd"], "format": "svg" }
]
```

Alternatively, switch to the bundled theme with **Preferences: File Icon
Theme** → **Maned Icons**. Be aware that it styles `.mnd` only, so every other
file loses its icon — the association above is usually the better trade.

## Supported platforms

| | Requirement |
|---|---|
| macOS | 11 Big Sur or newer. One universal binary covers Apple Silicon and Intel. |
| Linux x86-64 | glibc 2.35 or newer — Ubuntu 22.04+, Debian 12+, Fedora 36+ |
| Linux ARM64 | glibc 2.35 or newer |

**Windows is not supported.** Use WSL, where the Linux x86-64 build works
unchanged.

**Alpine and other musl systems are not supported.** The binaries link glibc.
The installer detects musl and tells you rather than installing something that
cannot run.

## Troubleshooting

### The command is not found

The install directory is not on your `PATH`. The installer prints the exact
line to add; it is usually:

```sh
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
```

Add it to `~/.zshrc` (macOS default), `~/.bashrc` (most Linux), or
`~/.config/fish/config.fish`, then open a new terminal.

### macOS says "Apple could not verify this app"

This only happens if you downloaded a tarball **with a browser**. macOS marks
browser downloads as quarantined, and these binaries are ad-hoc signed rather
than notarized. Clear the flag on the unpacked folder:

```sh
xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine .
```

The `curl` installer is unaffected — `curl` does not set the quarantine flag.

### "checksum mismatch"

The download was corrupted or truncated. Run the installer again. If it keeps
happening, please [open an issue](https://github.com/FabianoDicheti/maned/issues)
with the expected and actual hashes it printed.

### Permission denied writing to /usr/local/bin

Install into your home directory instead:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://fabianodicheti.github.io/maned/install.sh | sh -s -- --prefix ~/.local
```

The installer deliberately never escalates privileges on its own.

## Upgrading and removing

```sh
# upgrade: re-run the installer, it replaces what is there
curl -fsSL https://fabianodicheti.github.io/maned/install.sh | sh

# remove
curl -fsSL https://fabianodicheti.github.io/maned/install.sh | sh -s -- --uninstall
```

Uninstall only removes a file that identifies itself as the tool it is named
after, so it will not delete something it did not install.
